decisions.decision: Which bootstrap writes does this plan make safe?
decisions.ruling: All of vwf and stackgen, under one rule: every bootstrap config set, config unset, add tool, remove tool and --answer line in plugins/vwf/skills, plugins/stackgen/skills and plugins/vwf/assets (D18) that carries a value or a name. The three lines of gap G2 (setup migrate-pipeline.md:121, :204 and onboard-pipeline.md:157) are among them.
decisions.rejected: Setup only, the rest parked; the three lines of G2 only.

decisions.decision: Where does the one rule live?
decisions.ruling: In a new section, headed exactly ## Passing values, of plugins/vwf/assets/bootstrap-contract.md and plugins/stackgen/assets/bootstrap-contract.md, with the same body in both copies, placed after ## The calls the plugins use and before any later section. Every skill line cites it by that heading, through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/assets/bootstrap-contract.md of its own plugin.
decisions.rejected: A new vwf-only asset, stackgen left as it is.

decisions.decision: Which values must a skill quote?
decisions.ruling: Every value, always, whatever its source: the value argument of bootstrap config set and every value of an --answer <tool>.<key>=<value> pair. Serialize a list or a table value as JSON; pass a scalar, free text included, as its raw text, never encoded as a JSON string (D25). Then replace each ' with '\'' and wrap the whole value in single quotes. Never pass it unquoted or in double quotes. For --answer, quote the whole <tool>.<key>=<value> argument as one single-quoted word.
decisions.rejected: Quote only values from a cloned repo or free text, leaving enums and constants bare.

decisions.decision: What does the rule do with names that build a key path or a tool name?
decisions.ruling: Check them, and stop on a bad one. A name that becomes one segment of a key path contains only letters, digits, _ and -; a . is not allowed, because it splits the path into a nested key. The key shapes are: repo.members.<name>, the <field> of repo.members.<name>.<field>, repo.projects.<name>, the name of config unset repo.projects.<old name>, tools.<tool>.projects, releases.<key>, and the <env> and <project> of repo.deploy.<env>.<project>. A tool name given to add tool or remove tool is also a name of bootstrap catalog --json data.tools. A bad name stops that one write with a report that names it, and nothing is written for it. A . stays allowed inside a JSON value, for example the <name>@<marketplace> keys of tools.claude.plugins.project in materialize.md step 3.
decisions.rejected: Quote the whole key argument the same way as a value, with no check.

decisions.decision: Does the rule cover commands printed for the user to run by hand?
decisions.ruling: Yes, with the same quoting and the same name check: setup migrate-pipeline.md:210, execute land.md:113, and the remedy text that doctor's stack.mjs builds. The user copies and runs them.
decisions.rejected: Only the two printed lines in .md files; stack.mjs left as a parked gap.

decisions.decision: What does doctor's project-folder remedy show when the project name fails the D4 check?
decisions.ruling: The row stays as it is (rule project-folder, severity degraded), but its remedy prints no command. It reads: project <name> is not a valid bootstrap key (letters, digits, _ and - only); rename the project by hand in docs/blueprint/registry.yaml and in each projects.<name> key of .config/vwf.yaml, then run /vwf:setup and /vwf:doctor again (D21, D32). A valid name keeps today's remedy, bootstrap config set repo.projects.<name> '{"folder":"<path>"}' --json, where <path> stays a literal placeholder.
decisions.rejected: Print the command with the key single-quoted and escaped.

decisions.decision: Does this change plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes, one, U5 in wave 2, covering U1 to U4 and U8 (D24). U4 changes stack.mjs, a shipped script that runs, and the plan is a security fix.
decisions.rejected: The wave review only.

decisions.decision: Execution mode.
decisions.ruling: teams. Wave 1 holds four edit units; U2 and U3 cite the section that U1 writes, so they can agree on its heading and wording while they work.
decisions.rejected: solo, with the heading fixed in the rulings and the wave review catching a difference.

decisions.decision: Backlog and gaps.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 1: K2 compared the sed range, which takes the next heading of vwf copy only, and used <(...), which fish lacks.
decisions.ruling: K2 runs in bash -c and compares only the section body, from the ## Passing values heading to the line before the next ## heading or the end of the file (awk range).
decisions.rejected: Drop K2 and leave the comparison to the wave review.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 10: how does bootstrap config set store a single-quoted value?
decisions.ruling: Checked in a scratch repo on 2026-11-23: the shell removes the single quotes, so bootstrap gets the same string. config set repo.topology_reason with the value it's a "test"; $(echo hi) stored that exact text and ran nothing; a JSON object value is parsed into a table; the scalar 42 is stored as the string "42". Quoting changes no stored value.
decisions.rejected: none: a fact, not a choice

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 2: U3 quoted a D4 with repo.deploy and without tools.<tool>.projects.
decisions.ruling: D4 holds one full list of key shapes, repo.deploy.<env>.<project> included, and U1, U2 and U3 quote it word for word.
decisions.rejected: Leave repo.deploy out; the deploy URL is quoted as a value but env and project are not checked.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 3: doctor stack.mjs:248 prints bootstrap add tool ${tool} from a materialized entry tools: list, with no check.
decisions.ruling: U4 also checks the tool name of the tool-link remedy with /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/. A name that fails gets no command: the remedy says that tool <name> is not a valid bootstrap tool name. The row stays as it is. Doctor makes no bootstrap catalog call for this check.
decisions.rejected: Check against bootstrap catalog --json (one more bootstrap read in doctor); leave the tool-link remedy out of scope.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 4: doctor/references/stack-checks.md:71 and assets/vwf-config.md:195 give the repo.projects fix that D6 makes false for a bad name, and no unit owned them.

decisions.rejected: Add the two files to the docs unit U6.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 5: init/SKILL.md:424 runs bootstrap migrate with --answer, in a step no edit listed.
decisions.ruling: U3 quotes it too, per D3: every --answer of bootstrap migrate and of add tool.
decisions.rejected: Leave line 424 as an accepted case.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 6: printed bootstrap add tool <tool> fixes at setup/SKILL.md:339, migrate-pipeline.md:170, topology-detection.md:61 and doctor/references/stack-checks.md:95 and :111 had no unit.
decisions.ruling: D4 and D5 cover them as forms, per D20: each cites ## Passing values once, and the D4 check applies to the real name that fills the placeholder. U2 takes the setup lines and owns topology-detection.md; U8 takes stack-checks.md:95 and :111.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 7: materialize.md:154 writes tools.<t>.projects, a D4 key shape, with no check; does step 3 stay separate?

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 8: assets/stack-adapter.md:362, assets/vwf-config.md:152 and assets/topologies/monorepo.md:93 run bootstrap config set with values, outside D1 scope.
decisions.ruling: D1 also covers plugins/vwf/assets. U8 owns stack-adapter.md and topologies/monorepo.md too, and quotes each write with a citation of ## Passing values. K1 also searches plugins/vwf/assets and plugins/stackgen/assets; the hits inside the Passing values section itself are the rule.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 9: the sentence near the top of each bootstrap-contract.md copy names only the pane exception, but vwf also has the section ## The git ports that stackgen lacks.
decisions.ruling: U1 changes that sentence in both copies so that it names both differences: the pane exception and ## The git ports. index.md facts are corrected.
decisions.rejected: Correct only the index.md facts.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gaps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8: what do the rule and K1 do with a command that shows only placeholders?
decisions.ruling: A command that shows only placeholders (for example bootstrap add tool <tool>) is a form, not a write. In a .md file it cites ## Passing values once at the form, and whoever fills it in applies the rule; the D4 check applies to the real name, not to the placeholder. A script that prints a literal placeholder (doctor stack.mjs:421, the language-tool remedy) stays as it is. The call list of ## The calls the plugins use in both contract copies is the rule's own text. K1 accepts all three. U8 owns assets/stack-vocabulary.md and cites the rule at its line 39, and at vwf-config.md:924 (the 27 to 28 add tool fix) and vwf-config.md:901 (the 26 to 27 config set of member, env and project names, a real write: quoted per D3 and checked per D4).
decisions.rejected: A separate ruling for each placeholder line.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 5: the D6 remedy said rename it in .config/vwf.yaml, but doctor reads the project name from docs/blueprint/registry.yaml.
decisions.ruling: The remedy says: rename the project by hand in docs/blueprint/registry.yaml and in each projects.<name> key of .config/vwf.yaml, then run /vwf:setup and /vwf:doctor again (amended by D32: /vwf:architecture has no rename step).
decisions.rejected: Name registry.yaml only, for an edit by hand.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 6: a key of .config/releases.yaml fails the D4 check during the landing move in execute land.md:90-113.
decisions.ruling: Skip only that key and report it; write the valid keys. Do not remove .config/releases.yaml while it holds a skipped key, so the key is not lost. The landing continues.
decisions.rejected: Treat a bad key as a failed call, so step 5 abandons the whole move.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 7: a member, env or project name fails the D4 check during the 26 to 27 or 27 to 28 migration step of setup.
decisions.ruling: Check every name of the step before its first write. On a bad name, stop the migration step for that repo before any write: report the bad name and how to rename it. vwf.yaml keeps the key and the stamp stays at the old config_format, so the next /vwf:setup offers the step again. Other repos continue.
decisions.rejected: Skip only that key, keep it in vwf.yaml, and stamp the new format.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 9: D7 named U1 to U4 while U5 also covers U8, and U5 focus named only plugins/*/skills.
decisions.ruling: D7 names U1 to U4 and U8. U5 focus adds plugins/vwf/assets and the D20, D22 and D23 rulings.
decisions.rejected: Keep the review on plugins/*/skills and stack.mjs only.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 1: is a free-text scalar encoded as a JSON string before it is quoted?
decisions.ruling: No. A scalar is passed as its raw text; only a list or a table value is encoded as JSON. Checked in a scratch repo on 2026-11-23: for a string key, bootstrap stored [wip] text, {x} and ["a","b"] as the raw strings, and stored "quoted" with its double quotes, so a JSON-encoded scalar would store the extra quotes.
decisions.rejected: Encode every value as JSON.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 2: do the stack.mjs remedy templates at about lines 248 and 403 pass K1?
decisions.ruling: Yes. K1 accepts a script remedy that prints a command only after the D6 or D13 name check, when the tests prove the check. K1 names stack.mjs:248 and :403.
decisions.rejected: U7 reports them as K1 failures.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 3: prose that names a bootstrap write with no command line (setup/SKILL.md:253, setup/references/workspace-structure.md:27, assets/stack-vocabulary.md:21, stackgen materializer.md:114, stackgen-stack-template/SKILL.md:244, stackgen assets/pack-format.md:62).
decisions.ruling: A sentence that names a write without the command line the model runs is a mention. The rule applies at the step that holds the command. K1 accepts these six lines, and the run report names each one. No unit edits them.
decisions.rejected: Treat each as a form that cites the rule, with a new stackgen owner.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 4: the rename route that the D23 report gives for a bad member name or a bad deploy env name.
decisions.ruling: Member and env names still sit in .config/vwf.yaml before the step moves them. The report says to rename the name in .config/vwf.yaml by hand (for a submodule member, also its name in .gitmodules), then run /vwf:setup again. A bad project name uses the D21 route, /vwf:architecture.
decisions.rejected: Report the bad name and its key with no rename route.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 5: does the hand-step report of execute land.md:113 print a config set line for a releases key that D22 skipped?
decisions.ruling: No. For a skipped key the report prints no command: it names the key, says that it is not a valid bootstrap key, and says that it stays in .config/releases.yaml.
decisions.rejected: Print the line with the key quoted.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, gap 1: the escape is safe only in POSIX shells; in fish a backslash inside single quotes escapes the next quote, so a value with a backslash breaks the quoting (tested 2026-11-23: fish failed to parse the line, sh and zsh kept it one string).
decisions.ruling: A value that holds a backslash, a newline or another control character stops that one write with a report that names the key, and nothing is written for it. Without these characters the quote-escape form is the same in sh, bash, zsh and fish.
decisions.rejected: Run every bootstrap write inside /bin/sh -c; accept the fish case as an open gap.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, gap 2: after D22 skips a bad key of .config/releases.yaml, what happens to the moved valid keys?
decisions.ruling: The moved keys are removed from .config/releases.yaml, so only the skipped keys stay. The landing commit carries the edited file. Each later landing reports the same skip until the user renames the key; no key is written twice.
decisions.rejected: Keep the file whole, so each later landing moves the same keys again.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, gap 3: /vwf:architecture has no step that renames a project, so the route of D6, D21 and D28 does not exist.
decisions.ruling: The remedy and the reports say: rename the project by hand in docs/blueprint/registry.yaml and in each projects.<name> key of .config/vwf.yaml, then run /vwf:setup and /vwf:doctor again. A parked gap, docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-25-architecture-has-no-project-rename-parked.md, records that architecture has no rename step.
decisions.rejected: Name no route; keep through /vwf:architecture as an open gap.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, gap 4: does D3 encode an --answer list or table as JSON? Only config set was tested, and bootstrap help gives no list form for --answer.
decisions.ruling: No. An --answer value is never encoded as JSON. It is passed in the form that bootstrap questions --json shows for that question, then the whole <tool>.<key>=<value> argument is quoted per D3 and checked per D30. JSON encoding applies to config set only.
decisions.rejected: Keep D3 as it is and record the --answer list form as an open gap.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, gap 5: init/references/new-repo.md:65 is prose (add tool virajp-plugins --json --dry-run, then --yes with the answers) with no --answer argument to quote.
decisions.ruling: U3 adds a short clause at with the answers: each answer is passed as a quoted --answer per ## Passing values, so the line agrees with init/SKILL.md.
decisions.rejected: Treat it as a D27 mention.
